- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce peak forecasts by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising sharply, cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent high to prevent overshoot.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > true), apply a 1–3 day mean reversion correction downward, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates mid-range values (e.g., 72–74) while true values are anchored near 70–73, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8) and forecast shows erratic swings, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values before projecting.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect mean reversion.
